messages.content: What's the name of a type of cell that has multiple nuclei?

function.name: bloodcell_classification
function.description: Identify and categorize different types of blood cells based on given attributes. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

cell_shape.description: The shape of the cell, e.g. round, oval.

cell_size.description: The size of the cell, e.g. large, medium, small.

cell_function.description: The function of the cell, e.g. carrying oxygen, fighting infection. Default: 'carry oxygen'.

For example, skeletal muscle fibers (myocytes) are multinucleated. Also osteoclasts are multinucleated. But the user likely expects "multinucleated cell" or "polyploid cell". But we need to use the function. The function signature: bloodcell_classification takes an object with keys: cell_shape (string), cell_size (string), cell_function? (string). We need to provide these. The function returns any. We need to call it. Let's choose a typical multinucleated cell: skeletal muscle fiber. So shape: elongated, size: large, function: contract muscle. But the function default is 'carry oxygen', but we can override. So we call with cell_shape: "elongated", cell_size: "large", cell_function: "contract muscle". That will return something.
